title: 36.6 A 112Gb/s 0.61pJ/b PAM-4 Linear TIA Supporting Extended PD-TIA Reach in 28nm CMOS
problem: Co-packaged optical receivers require extended photodiode-to-TIA reach (0.2 inch vs. 0.03 inch in prior work) for thermal, mechanical, and field-replacement flexibility, but long interconnects introduce signal reflection, in-band amplitude un-flatness, and bandwidth degradation.
motivation: Cloud storage and AI applications drive higher data rates and integration density via co-packaging, requiring TIA designs that tolerate extended PD-TIA distances without area/power penalties.
method: A 4×112Gb/s PAM-4 linear TIA employs active-input-termination (AIT-TIA) to suppress reflection and signal-interpolation-based single-ended-to-differential converter (S2D) for enhanced bandwidth. These techniques extend achievable PD-TIA reach to 0.2 inch with 0.61pJ/b energy efficiency in 28nm CMOS.
key_novelty: Active-input-termination TIA with signal-interpolation S2D converter enabling 0.2-inch PD-TIA reach while maintaining low power efficiency (0.61pJ/b).
contributions: Extends PD-TIA reach to 0.2 inch (6.7× improvement over prior 0.03-inch limit)
4-channel receiver integration in 28nm CMOS for co-packaging applications
baselines: Prior work with 0.03-inch PD-TIA reach using damping resistors
limitations: Not discussed; temperature stability, jitter performance, and noise figure over extended reach not fully characterized.
primary_theme: Extended-reach TIA via active input termination
